title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: grower agronomist assembling covariates trial site asks plain question: one exact paddock, can pull daily temperature rainfall, vegetation index, district farm economics several public archives, one interface, get back tidy table carries source, licence retrieval time, without leaking paddock’s exact coordinates without live network connection standing reproducing analysis next season? vignette answers terroir’s shipped fixtures, offline throughout, closes happens source answer .

title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: terroir pulls climate, weather, vegetation-index, soil, elevation agricultural-economics data single geographic point many free sources, behind one uniform request--response contract. data-collector member ORCHESTRA: producer feeds covariates forcings downstream modelling. Every source optional adapter, terroir installs works none source packages present. geo_point_request() builds request: point, optional date range, variables wanted, id one registered source. list_sources() lists every registered adapter, register_source() adds one, enforcing data-collector role’s free-rule – adapter reach free source refused registration time, discovered later billing surprise. collect_point() dispatches one request adapter returns verified geo_point_series, structured refusal source unknown, package missing, point falls outside source’s declared coverage, returned value fails plausibility check. collect_points() runs whole batch requests keeps every refusal accounted row rather dropping stack. is_refusal() is_replayed() tell two special outcomes apart ordinary series; verify_geo_series() geo_point_schema() contract , exported downstream package can check type directly rather reaching terroir’s internals.

text: toy adapter returns constant value illustration; real adapter call upstream package instead, way built-sources . free-rule enforced, merely stated: registering adapter free = FALSE refused outright, refusal names rule enforces.
code: toy_adapter <- function(request, retrieved_at) {   dt <- data.table::data.table(     date = request$start, variable = "toy_index", value = 1   )   new_geo_point_series(     dt, lon = request$lon, lat = request$lat, source = "toy_local",     source_version = "1.0", license = "CC0", retrieved_at = retrieved_at,     call = "toy_adapter()"   ) } register_source(   "toy_local", toy_adapter, package = "base", free = TRUE,   description = "Illustrative in-memory adapter used only in this vignette" ) "toy_local" %in% list_sources()$id #> [1] TRUE free_only_refusal <- tryCatch(   register_source("toy_paid", toy_adapter, package = "base", free = FALSE),   error = function(e) conditionMessage(e) ) cat(free_only_refusal) #> Refusing to register "toy_paid": the data-collector role is free-only. #> ℹ Every adapter must reach a free source (`free = TRUE`).

title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: terroir ships small set recorded fixtures, one per CORE source. Passing offline = TRUE answers request matching fixture network egress – useful reproducible pipeline, continuous-integration run, (coarsening, ) sovereign coordinate must never reach upstream service. replayed series carries replayed = TRUE provenance keeps recording’s retrieved_at, consumer can always tell cached series live one. Offline mode needs none source packages installed: reads .rds fixtures never touches adapter. recorded fixture answers request, offline mode returns structured refusal rather silently falling back network – zero-egress guarantee absolute. caller can point terroir directory recorded fixtures options(terroir.fixture_dir = "/path//fixtures"), switch whole session offline options(terroir.offline = TRUE).

title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: grower’s exact paddock GPS sensitive. point flagged sovereign = TRUE, terroir coarsens coordinate roughly one-kilometre cell upstream call, exact location never leaves host. raw-requested coarsened-sent coordinate recorded provenance – host keeps full record, upstream service sees coarsened point. Coarsening also available non-sovereign point via coarsen argument: single number rounds many degrees precision (example coarsen = 0.01 roughly 1 km cell), coarsen = list(grid = 0.25) snaps coordinate nearest quarter-degree grid node. returned series’ provenance gains sovereign, coarsen_policy, raw-vs-sent coordinates; fixed ten-column series schema unchanged, consumer reading columns unaffected.
code: sovereign_req <- geo_point_request(   lon = 138.63124, lat = -34.92871,   # an exact paddock GPS   start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-31",   source = "nasapower",   sovereign = TRUE                    # coarsening on by default ) sovereign_req       # prints both the raw and the coarsened (sent) point #> <geo_point_request> source "nasapower" #> point: (138.63, -34.93) range: 2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-31 #> variables: (adapter default) #> coarsened (sovereign): raw (138.63124, -34.92871) -> sent (138.63, -34.93) #> policy "precision=0.01"

title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: collect_points() runs several requests stacks outcomes one table, tagged request_index status column. refusal contributes exactly one accounted row rather disappearing stack, multi-site collection dead source still reports every request given. One row per request three-request batch (n = 41 stacked rows total).
code: batch_reqs <- list(   geo_point_request(     138.6, -34.92, "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10",     variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"), source = "nasapower"   ),   geo_point_request(140.7, -35.30, source = "abares"),   geo_point_request(0, 0, source = "not_a_source") ) batch_out <- collect_points(batch_reqs, offline = TRUE) batch_summary <- batch_out[, .(   source = source[1L], status = status[1L], n_rows = .N,   reason = reason[1L] ), by = request_index]

title: Collecting geo-point data with terroir
text: 12 sources currently registered, free construction: free-rule tested refuses paid adapter explicit error rather letting one slip registry silently. Air temperature Adelaide across replayed ten days ranges 15.50 31.06 degC – day--day swing typical Adelaide midsummer front moves – precipitation essentially dry: 2 ten days record trace (0.03 0.06 mm), rest zero. collector returned flat temperature line wet run days signal distrust fixture trusting anything built top . Coarsening moves sovereign point exact (138.63124, -34.92871) sent (138.63, -34.93) precision=0.01 policy – roughly one-kilometre cell latitude – coarsened point, never exact paddock GPS, reaches upstream service. three-request batch stacks 41 rows: two answerable requests (nasapower, abares) contribute one row per collected value, one unregistered source contributes exactly one refused row rather dropped, carrying reason reason column rather bare NA.

title: Construct a geo-point data request — geo_point_request
text: lon, lat Numeric scalars. Longitude latitude WGS84 decimal degrees (EPSG:4326). lon [-180, 180], lat [-90, 90]. start, end Character scalars (ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD") NULL. inclusive date range. Ignored static layers (example soil elevation). variables Character vector source-native variable names, NULL let adapter choose sensible defaults. source Character scalar. id one registered source adapter (see list_sources()). sovereign Logical scalar. TRUE, point treated sensitive (sovereign-data coordinate – grower's paddock, trial site) coarsening applied default exact GPS never leaves host (see coarsen). Defaults FALSE. coarsen Coordinate-coarsening policy applied lon/lat upstream call, exact coordinate never transmitted. One : NULL (coarsening; default non-sovereign point); single positive number giving rounding precision degrees (example 0.01 rounds roughly 1 km cell); list(grid = <size>) snapping coordinate nearest multiple <size> degrees. sovereign = TRUE point coarsen = NULL, default precision 0.01 degrees applied automatically. request records raw-requested coordinate coarsened-sent coordinate.

title: Construct a geo-point data request — geo_point_request

title: Register a data-source adapter — register_source
text: id Character scalar. Unique source id (used source geo_point_request()). fun function function(request, retrieved_at) returning geo_point_series. package Character scalar. upstream package adapter needs (declared Suggests; checked collect time). free Logical scalar. Must TRUE – free-role rule. description Character scalar. One-line description. extent Optional numeric c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) WGS84 giving source's valid spatial extent, NULL global source. request outside declared extent refused collect_point() rather silently returning --coverage value (Independent Oracle Principle: Australia-source must queried Argentina). batch Optional function function(requests, retrieved_at) answers many requests source one upstream call. returns list length requests, element geo_point_series refusal. collect_points() uses raster sources, one file read serves every point. Retrieval provenance ocular series. Beyond contract’s five provenance fields, ocular series carries STAC endpoint collection id, resolved sensor, index name, window size, scene-level cloud ceiling, mask asset / kind / class set, scene dates, scene ids ocular commit actually installed (read ocular’s DESCRIPTION, drifted install visible rather assumed). Scene ids read verbatim returned asset URLs – ocular’s scene records retain STAC item id – NA identifier present; signed URLs never recorded. Unmaskable scene refuses. scene whose STAC item carries SCL / QA_PIXEL asset cloud-masked; adapter refuses (naming scene date missing asset) rather returning unmasked inside series advertised cloud-masked. Refusal, abort, implausible value. collect_point()’s value-plausibility conformer (--range NDVI/EVI temperature) now returns structured terroir_refusal instead aborting call, one bad cell longer stops whole collection. verify_geo_series() called directly unchanged still aborts.
